html:
Usman dan Fodio was a Fulani Muslim scholar and preacher who led a holy war against the Hausa kings and founded the Sokoto Caliphate, in what is now northern Nigeria.

He was born in the Hausa kingdom of Gobir to a family of Fulani scholars. From the 1770s he preached across the Hausa states against unjust taxes, corrupt courts and the mixing of Islam with older beliefs, and he drew a large following of Fulani herders and Hausa peasants. As his movement grew, the king of Gobir turned against him.

In 1804 he withdrew with his followers to Gudu, was proclaimed Commander of the Faithful, and declared jihad. By 1808 Gobir's capital had fallen. His flag-bearers carved out emirates such as Kano, Zaria and Katsina, and the jihad pushed on toward Bornu and Yorubaland. The result, also called the Fulani Empire, became one of the largest states in Africa.

He left the ruling to his son Muhammad Bello and his brother Abdullahi and went back to teaching and writing. He wrote more than a hundred works in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa. His daughter Nana Asma'u carried on his work as a poet and teacher of women. His jihad was one of a chain of Fula-led Islamic revolutions in West Africa, after the Futa Jallon jihad.
sum: Usman dan Fodio was a Fulani Muslim scholar and preacher who led a holy war against the Hausa kings and founded the Sokoto Caliphate, in what is now northern Nigeria.
